dinkum-3.meaning: Every instruction survives: "pull the pin on things or put 'em off early", "A solid building or a car with a hard roof is a safe bet. Rain shelters, little sheds and open vehicles aren't.", "wait 30 minutes after the last lightnin' or thunder", "they're safe to touch".
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "power point", "Mobiles", "cops a lightnin' strike", "give ya a squiz", "quick smart". "Mobiles and cordless phones are right." strains, since bare "are right" for "are safe" is unusual outside "she'll be right".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural: "leave it way too late", "when there's thunderstorms about", "a thunderstorm's brewin'", "Gettin' Yer Head Round the Threat". "every bloke and sheila" is a stock phrase.
dinkum-3.register: A full Aussie retelling of every paragraph ("Best way to look after yerself with lightnin'? Don't be anywhere near it.") with no swearing, which is within vulgarity 2; the right weight for a level-5 brief.
dinkum-3.tone: Stays an urgent, plain safety warning: "get inside somewhere safe straight away", "Call 911 and keep an eye on 'em."
dinkum-3.flow: Reads well aloud: "Keep an eye on the weather and get yerself somewhere safe before it turns nasty." Some repeats of "carry on" and "about" ("how they carry on when thunderstorms are about", "how you carry on when thunderstorms are about").
dinkum-3.variety: Varied: "pull the pin", "squiz", "cops", "quick smart", "brewin'", "turns nasty"; "about" and "leave it way too late" recur.
dinkum-3.essence: Clearly the lightning-safety notice, with its slogan, structure and headings retold: "When Thunder Roars, Go Indoors!"

engine.meaning: Nearly verbatim, so every point is kept, including the source slip "what can do to lower their risk" and "when thunderstorm are in the area".
engine.sense: The few substitutions fit: "power point", "Mobiles and cordless phones are safe", "behaviour".
engine.authenticity: Little Aussie beyond spelling and dropped letters, and what there is is pasted on: "'ave a lightning safety plan", "struck by lightning'n what can do", "every bloke'n sheila".
engine.register: Largely untranslated for a level-5 brief: "Monitor weather conditions and get to a safe place before the weather becomes threatenin'." "In the first graph, the threat of lightning increases as a thunderstorm approaches" is the original word for word.
engine.tone: Keeps the original's plain warning tone since it is the original: "If someone is struck by lightning, they may need immediate medical attention."
engine.flow: Clunky joins from contractions forced onto formal prose: "why and when people are struck by lightning'n what can do", "keep away from outside doors and windows'n don't lie", "'ave a lightning safety plan".
engine.variety: The little slang there is is one device repeated: "'n" joins ("windows'n doors", "bloke'n sheila") and dropped g ("lightnin'").
engine.essence: Recognisably the notice in full, but with nothing of a retelling it stays the source text with blemishes.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All points survive: "call off or put off whatever you've got on, early, if storms are forecast", "open-top vehicles are not safe", "wait 30 minutes after the last lightnin' or thunder", "so they're safe to touch".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Each term fits: "power point", "Mobiles", "mucking about like that is behind heaps of the lightnin' deaths", "copping a deadly strike", "quick smart".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like a local: "when there's thunderstorms about", "the sky's lookin' ugly", "Gettin' Your Head Round the Threat". "every bloke and sheila" is stock.
yarn-dinkum.register: Fully retold at level 5 ("Too many people leave it far too bloody late"), with mild swearing well within vulgarity 2.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Remains a serious safety message: "If someone's been struck by lightnin', they might need medical help straight away."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads smoothly: "Some hang about till the storm's right overhead and it's started to rain."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "mucking about", "steer clear", "copping", "quick smart", "blows in", "lookin' ugly"; "about"/"around" for storms recurs ("when there's storms about", "when a storm's around").
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the NWS lightning notice with its slogan and sections, retold.

yarn-troppo.meaning: All instructions kept, with emphatic asides that hang off the original: "Nowhere.", "Don't kid yerself.", "Thirty minutes, the full half hour.", "Don't hang back."
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "cops a lightnin' strike", "Some duck inside the minute a storm shows its face", "could get a jolt through it from a strike nearby", "quick smart".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian talking: "No word of a lie", "hands off anythin' plugged into a power point", "Yer mobile and the cordless are fine", "no muckin' about".
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-5 telling throughout ("A proper solid buildin' or a car with a hard roof, they're yer safe bets."), with only "far too bloody late" as swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: The urgency is kept and even heightened ("Thirty minutes, the full half hour."); "close enough for that storm to reach out and get ya" edges towards playful.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads like it was spoken: "Rain shelters, little sheds and open-top vehicles? Not safe. Don't kid yerself."
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range, nothing leaned on: "No word of a lie", "dawdlin'", "duck inside", "shows its face", "a jolt", "no muckin' about", "don't hang back".
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the safety notice, its slogan and its stepwise advice, told as a yarn.

unharnessed.meaning: Points kept, but "Rain shelters, little sheds and open vehicles are bloody useless." shifts "not safe" to "useless", and "it starts bucketing down" turns starting rain into a downpour.
unharnessed.sense: "bloody useless" strains for "not safe", and "It's all this dodgy behaviour" pulls "unsafe" toward shady; otherwise apt: "on the cards", "cops a lightning strike", "quick smart".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural Aussie without spelt-out accent: "Way too many people muck about", "that dragging of the feet", "through piss-poor planning", "the sky's looking angry".
unharnessed.register: Retold throughout with swearing within vulgarity 2 ("piss-poor planning", "drop a hell of a lot"); a little short of a full level-5 yarn, keeping headings like "Minimizing the Risk".
unharnessed.tone: The warning stays a warning, though swearing ("far too bloody long", "piss-poor planning") makes it read as a scolding in places.
unharnessed.flow: Mostly smooth: "Keep an eye on the weather and get yourself somewhere safe before it turns nasty." "harm's way" and "when there's storms about" repeat ("stay out of harm's way", "puts people in harm's way").
unharnessed.variety: Varied: "have a crack", "muck about", "on the cards", "bucketing down", "piss-poor", "dodgy"; "when there's storms about" repeats three times.
unharnessed.essence: Recognisably the notice; a little sharpened toward a telling-off.

dinkum-3.quote: Mobiles and cordless phones are right.
dinkum-3.original: Cell phones and cordless phones are safe.
dinkum-3.why: Bare "are right" for "are safe" is unusual; "are fine" or "are right to use" is what a local would say.

H-dropping in writing reads as Cockney pastiche, not Australian.

unharnessed.quote: Rain shelters, little sheds and open vehicles are bloody useless.
unharnessed.original: Rain shelters, small sheds, and open vehicles are not safe.
unharnessed.why: "Useless" is not "unsafe"; it changes a safety claim into a general put-down.

unharnessed.original: It is all of these unsafe behaviors
unharnessed.why: "Dodgy" suggests dishonest or shonky, not risky.
Overstates the trigger; the point is that people wait for rain at all.
US spelling left in the heading.

summaries.dinkum-3: A faithful, natural and full retelling that keeps the warning serious; a few stock or odd touches.
summaries.engine: Essentially the original with a few spelling changes and pasted-on contractions; far too light for the brief.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Faithful, natural and smooth, with the warning kept serious and the brief met.
summaries.yarn-troppo: The fullest and most natural telling, keeping every instruction and the urgency.
summaries.unharnessed: Natural, punchy and within the brief, with one safety claim bent ("bloody useless") and a scolding edge.
